newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV shares off highs after quality results.
newsitem.headline: BBV shares off highs after quality results.

text.p: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya shares were firmer but off earlier highs on Thursday, after the bank announced a 24 percent rise in 1996 profit, just above analyst expectations.
"These are spectacular, and I would highlight above all the quality of the figures with strength in the recurrent earnings line," said a dealer at a Spanish bank.
At 1305 GMT, BBV was up 20 pesetas to 7,900, off an earlier high of 7,970. The Ibex-35 index of leading stocks was down 2.15 points, 0.04 percent to 5,460.92.
BBV posted a rise in 1996 net attributable profit to 104.26 billion pesetas from 84.01 billion in the previous year. Net interest income rose to 415.57 billion from 343.27 billion.
The stock fell after the results were released because the growth in profits had largely been expected, a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
"BBV's already had a really good run this month," he said.
But the Spanish bank dealer said there may be better things to come for the banking group.
"If there is a pick-up in the economy, its clear that BBV of all the banks stands to benefit most," she said.
It was particularly impressive that growth had not simply stemmed from an increase in atypicals, but rather from the core banking business itself, she said.
Analysts polled by Reuters earlier this week were expecting an average 23 percent rise in BBV profits.
